turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have sharp, knife-stroke pain on my forehead, left cheek, and left temple. It’s 7 out of 10 in intensity, and it starts very quickly—pace 10 out of 10.

How long does each pain attack last—seconds, minutes, or hours?
How long does each pain attack last—seconds, minutes, or hours?
Does the pain come in brief repeated bursts, or is it more continuous once it starts?
It comes in brief repeated bursts.
Are the bursts triggered by things like touching your face, chewing, talking, brushing teeth, or a cold breeze?
Do you get any eye redness or tearing, nasal congestion/runny nose, drooping eyelid, or sweating on that side during the attacks?
Is the pain always strictly on the left side, or does it ever switch sides?
It’s on the left side (forehead, left cheek, and left temple).
Any rash, blisters, or skin sensitivity on the left forehead/face, or any recent dental problem or sinus infection?
Any numbness, weakness, vision changes, fever, or pain with chewing?

[ABSTAIN] Insufficient discriminating information; key features like attack duration, triggers, autonomic symptoms, rash, and neurologic/red-flag symptoms are unknown.
[POSSIBLE] trigeminal neuralgia, cluster headache, paroxysmal hemicrania, herpes zoster involving trigeminal distribution, dental/sinus source of facial pain
